text_solutions.text:
"1. Question: What is the wavelength of the third line of the Balmer series for a hydrogen (H) atom?
2. Concepts:
  • Balmer Series: A series of spectral lines in the hydrogen spectrum that corresponds to electron transitions from higher energy levels (n > 2) to the n = 2 energy level. 
3. Formula: The Rydberg formula for wavelength (λ) is:1/λ = R × (1/n₁² - 1/n₂²)
4. Solution:
  • Third Line of Balmer Series: The third line corresponds to the transition from n = 5 to n = 2.
  • Substitute Values in Rydberg Formula:
    • n₁ = 2 (final energy level)
    • n₂ = 5 (initial energy level)
    • 1/λ = R × (1/2² – 1/5²)
  • Simplify and Solve for λ:
    • 1/λ = R × (1/4 – 1/25)
    • 1/λ = R × (21/100)
    • λ = 100 / 21R
Therefore, the wavelength of the third line of the Balmer series for a hydrogen atom is 100 / 21R."

  • Balmer Series: A series of spectral lines in the hydrogen spectrum that corresponds to electron transitions from higher energy levels (n > 2) to the n = 2 energy level. 
3. Formula: The Rydberg formula for wavelength (λ) is:1/λ = R × (1/n₁² - 1/n₂²)
4. Solution:
  • Third Line of Balmer Series: The third line corresponds to the transition from n = 5 to n = 2.
  • Substitute Values in Rydberg Formula:
    • n₁ = 2 (final energy level)
    • n₂ = 5 (initial energy level)
    • 1/λ = R × (1/2² – 1/5²)
  • Simplify and Solve for λ:
    • 1/λ = R × (1/4 – 1/25)
    • 1/λ = R × (21/100)
    • λ = 100 / 21R
Therefore, the wavelength of the third line of the Balmer series for a hydrogen atom is 100 / 21R."
